Let
\[
A_0=\begin{pmatrix}a&1\\-3&-2\end{pmatrix}
\]
be the spatially homogeneous ODE matrix. Its trace and determinant are
\[
\operatorname{tr}A_0=a-2,\qquad \det A_0=3-2a.
\]
Thus the ODE is exponentially stable iff
\[
0<a<\frac32.
\]

For Neumann frequency \(n\ge 1\), write
\[
q_n=\left(\frac{n\pi}{b}\right)^2.
\]
The mode matrix is
\[
A_n=\begin{pmatrix}a-q_n&1\\-3&-2-10q_n\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its trace is
\[
a-2-11q_n<0
\]
whenever \(0<a<3/2\). Hence a mode is unstable exactly when its determinant is negative:
\[
\det A_n
=(a-q_n)(-2-10q_n)+3
=10q_n^2+(2-10a)q_n+(3-2a)<0.
\]

The quadratic is negative between its two positive roots. Those roots exist precisely when
\[
25a^2+10a-29>0,
\]
so, together with ODE stability,
\[
\frac{\sqrt{30}-1}{5}<a<\frac32.
\]
Define
\[
\alpha=\frac{5a-1-\sqrt{25a^2+10a-29}}{10},\qquad
\beta=\frac{5a-1+\sqrt{25a^2+10a-29}}{10}.
\]
Then frequency \(n\ge1\) is unstable exactly when
\[
\alpha<\left(\frac{n\pi}{b}\right)^2<\beta,
\]
equivalently
\[
\frac{b\sqrt{\alpha}}{\pi}<n<\frac{b\sqrt{\beta}}{\pi}.
\]

Therefore the PDE has exactly three unstable nonconstant Neumann frequencies iff the open interval
\[
\left(\frac{b\sqrt{\alpha}}{\pi},\frac{b\sqrt{\beta}}{\pi}\right)
\]
contains exactly three positive integers.

Equivalently, the full answer is:

\[
\boxed{
\frac{\sqrt{30}-1}{5}<a<\frac32
}
\]
and there exists an integer \(m\ge1\) such that the three unstable frequencies are exactly
\[
m,\ m+1,\ m+2,
\]
i.e.
\[
\boxed{
m-1\le \frac{b\sqrt{\alpha}}{\pi}<m
\quad\text{and}\quad
m+2<\frac{b\sqrt{\beta}}{\pi}\le m+3.
}
\]

In terms of \(b\), this is
\[
\boxed{
\frac{(m-1)\pi}{\sqrt{\alpha}}\le b<\frac{m\pi}{\sqrt{\alpha}},
\qquad
\frac{(m+2)\pi}{\sqrt{\beta}}< b\le\frac{(m+3)\pi}{\sqrt{\beta}},
}
\]
for some integer \(m\ge1\), with \(\alpha,\beta\) as above.
